success_patterns: When an exponent is defined by a liminf, translate the claim back into quantified counting inequalities before comparing options: a lower exponent bound of α yields N^{α-o(1)}, not necessarily a fixed-constant bound cN^α.
Do not treat two differently worded options as equivalent merely because they share the same exponent; check whether one adds a uniform constant or stronger quantifier.

patch.reasoning: The growth-exponent trajectory highlights an important exact-comparison distinction: a liminf lower bound does not generally imply a constant-factor counting lower bound at the endpoint exponent. Adding this check helps avoid selecting a stronger formulation than the definition supports.

edits.content: For growth exponents defined by a liminf, translate the claim back into counting inequalities before comparing options: \(\liminf_{N\to\infty}\log A(N)/\log N\ge \alpha\) guarantees \(A(N)\ge N^{\alpha-o(1)}\), but not necessarily \(A(N)\ge cN^\alpha\) for a fixed \(c>0\). Check endpoint exponents and uniform constants rather than treating these formulations as equivalent.
